# DSP reference fixture

`prediction-spectrum-float.bin` and `prediction-spectrum-double.bin` use `LPS1`:
little-endian u32 scalar width and 48-case count. Each case has u32 bin count,
FFT length/order, input magnitudes, order+1 correlation values, order+1
coefficients, gain and full FFT-length prediction spectrum. Eleven resonance
cases follow with u32 coefficient count, coefficients, u32 pole count,
frequencies and interleaved selected real/imaginary poles. Each precision has
1560 output slots. Unmodified C reproduction, numeric bounds, corrected/Legacy
policies and independent checks are in `docs/prediction-spectrum-compatibility.md`.

`prediction-float.bin` and `prediction-double.bin` use `LPC1`: little-endian
u32 scalar width and 64-case count; each case stores u32 sample count/order,
sample-count waveform values, order+1 autocorrelation values, order+1
coefficient values and one gain. The source function bodies and headers are
unchanged. Each precision compares 1288 scalar outputs. See
`docs/prediction-compatibility.md` and `tests/generate_prediction_reference.py`.

`complex-float.bin` and `complex-double.bin` use `CPX1`: little-endian u32
scalar width and 64-case count; each case has four operand components, eight
complex outputs (conjugate, sum, difference, product, quotient, then levels
one/two/three of exp), and levels one/two of argument. A u32 count of fifteen
scalar cases follows, each holding a log operand and exponent, three logarithm
outputs, three exponential outputs, faster base-two log and faster base-two exp.
Each precision compares 1272 scalar output slots. The canonical files use
Windows Zig 0.16.0 and unmodified pinned C headers. Linux GCC checks all data
exactly except the measured host-dependent scalar double exp difference. See
`docs/complex-compatibility.md` and the reproducible generator/bounds oracle.

`vector-phase-float.bin` and `vector-phase-double.bin` use `VPH1`: little-endian
u32 scalar width and 24-case count, then each case's u32 length, real/imaginary/
angle input arrays and twelve output arrays in the order declared in
`tests/reference/vector_phase_oracle.c`. Eighteen grid records follow, containing
u32 count, scalar bounds, grid points, interpolation ratio and interpolated
value. Nine integer progression records contain u32 count, i32 starting value
and step, and i32 outputs. Each precision has 3954 scalar output slots and 45
integer outputs. The generator uses pinned unmodified C headers; Zig and GCC
produce identical bytes. Scalar complex helper aliases are checked against
array results inside the C oracle. See `docs/vector-phase-compatibility.md` for
corrected empty/range boundaries and explicit Legacy Nyquist behavior.

`statistics-float.bin` and `statistics-double.bin` use `STA1`: little-endian u32
scalar width and case count, followed by input length, lag count, both input
vectors, nine basic statistics, a correlation-valid flag and correlation value,
all selection ranks, sorted values, original sort indices and cross correlation.
Invalid correlation values use a zero placeholder. The only C source correction
is the finite-value sort comparator in `statistics-sort-correction.patch`.
See `docs/statistics-compatibility.md` for precision, IEEE edge handling and
generator commands.

The four `matrix-{legacy,corrected}-{float,double}.bin` fixtures use `MAT1`:
scalar width and correction flag, then counts of product, row-swap and LU cases,
all integers as little-endian u32. Product records store rows, inner size and
columns, both inputs, matrix product and vector product. Swap records store
rows, columns, input matrix/vector, ordered swap indices and both outputs.
LU records store order, original matrix/right-hand side, swaps, pivoted matrix,
permuted right-hand side, packed factors and solution. Floating payloads use
the header scalar width. See `docs/matrix-compatibility.md` for provenance,
corrections and reproduction commands.

`polynomial-float.bin` and `polynomial-double.bin` contain original-C polynomial
evaluations and roots in `POL1` format. The header stores scalar width and record
count as little-endian u32. Each record stores coefficient count, complex
coefficients, three argument/result pairs and degree-many roots, each complex
number as real/imaginary scalars. The trailing u32 count precedes 61 scalar
argument/sine/cosine triples. Float has 32 records and double has 33, including
one deliberately unconverged eight-root case. See
`docs/polynomial-compatibility.md` for algorithm limits and generator commands.

The `root-float.bin` and `root-double.bin` fixtures contain 25 scalar zero
searches each, generated from unmodified ciglet commit
`895ba9b1c0eabee83d3544208bbc82420efa3206`. The `ROT1` format stores the scalar
width and record count as little-endian u32, followed by each function ID,
lower/upper bound and result in the selected scalar width. GCC on Ubuntu and
Zig 0.16.0 on Windows produce identical bytes with `-O2` for these cases.
Regenerate with `tests/generate_root_reference.py --upstream PATH --check`.
Use `--cc zig --zig` on Windows. Both precision tests compare every root exactly.

`dsp-reference.txt` is generated by `tests/reference/dsp_oracle.c` against ciglet commit `895ba9b1c0eabee83d3544208bbc82420efa3206`, with GCC on Ubuntu x86_64 and `-DFP_TYPE=float -std=c99`, linking `-lm`. Values are printed with nine significant digits to preserve binary32 results on round-trip parsing.

This fixture checks vector statistics, six precise window functions, and frame padding. A maximum absolute error of `1e-7` passes the current Windows MSVC x86_64 and i686 comparisons. This is a scoped threshold for these inputs, not a tolerance claim covering all DSP algorithms or all input sizes.

Compile with `gcc -DFP_TYPE=float -std=c99 -I<upstream> tests/reference/dsp_oracle.c -lm -o dsp-oracle`, then capture `dsp-oracle` output. The fixture does not require linking the upstream library because these tested reference functions are inline definitions in `ciglet.h`.

Intentional corrections: empty statistical inputs return errors or `None`; invalid vector sizes return errors; singleton windows are unity instead of dividing by zero; sorting uses deterministic total ordering and preserves the original index order of equal values.

The FFT fixtures c-fft-f32.bin and c-fft-f64.bin use the pinned unmodified ciglet.c and external/fftsg_h.c compiled with FP_TYPE=float and FP_TYPE=double respectively. tests/reference/fft_oracle.c writes 240 records and 92,112 scalar outputs per precision. Cases cover lengths 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 256, 512, and 1024; impulses, deterministic complex signals, and large DC offsets; all four present/absent real/imaginary combinations; and both transform directions. The C build uses -O2 -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections -lm, without -Ofast or fast-math. Section removal allows unused ciglet subsystems to remain unlinked. No upstream source is modified.

Binary format: ASCII FFT1, little-endian uint32 scalar byte width and record count, then uint32 length/scenario/component-mask/inverse fields per record followed by interleaved real/imaginary scalars. This fixture is generated on Ubuntu x86_64, whose native byte order is little-endian; Rust decodes it explicitly.

Across Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686, all eight integration tests pass. Maximum absolute differences across these targets are 2.288818359375e-5 for f32 and 1.1368683772161603e-13 for f64. Errors normalized by max(1, maximum input component magnitude) times length for forward transforms, or by the same input magnitude for normalized inverse transforms, were at most 3.3527612686157227e-8 and 1.1102230246251565e-16 respectively. Acceptance thresholds are 2e-7 for f32 and 1e-15 for f64, allowing platform/backend variation while remaining close to measured errors. These are scoped kernel thresholds, not complete speech-feature or inference tolerances. Independent round-trip and Parseval checks validate normalization; frequency-shift checks cover odd/even/singleton/empty sequences against the original inline ordering.

The direct inverse DFT fixtures c-idft-f32.bin and c-idft-f64.bin use tests/reference/idft_oracle.c with the same pinned unmodified C source and compiler flags as the FFT oracle. A reproducible POSIX command from the crate root is shown below; set CIGLET_UPSTREAM to the pinned checkout and repeat with FP_TYPE=double for the f64 fixture. The IDF1 format uses the same field layout as FFT1, with 120 records and 3,552 scalar outputs per precision. Lengths 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 11, 16, 31, and 64 include non-power-of-two and prime cases, with the same three input families and four component-presence combinations. Every record uses the normalized inverse convention. Independent tests verify constant-spectrum cancellation, the positive imaginary sign of a known four-point inverse, all-zero absent inputs, and invalid shape/length errors. This implementation retains quadratic complexity and scalar arithmetic order; the FFT API remains available for power-of-two lengths.

```sh
gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -I"$CIGLET_UPSTREAM" tests/reference/idft_oracle.c "$CIGLET_UPSTREAM/ciglet.c" "$CIGLET_UPSTREAM/external/fftsg_h.c" -Wl,--gc-sections -lm -o idft-oracle
./idft-oracle tests/fixtures/c-idft-f32.bin
```

Across the five required native targets, the tested f32 inverse DFT values match C exactly. The largest observed f64 absolute difference is 1.1368683772161603e-13, with normalized error 5.551115123125783e-17. Acceptance thresholds are 2e-7 for f32 and 1e-15 for f64, using max(1, maximum input component magnitude) as the inverse-transform scale. These thresholds apply only to the recorded direct inverse DFT cases.

The DCT fixtures c-dct-f32.bin and c-dct-f64.bin use tests/reference/dct_oracle.c, the pinned unmodified C source, and the same section-removal build flags as the inverse DFT driver. Substitute dct_oracle.c and the matching executable/fixture names in the command above. DCT1 begins with a scalar byte width and record count as little-endian uint32 values. Each of the 32 records contains uint32 length/scenario fields followed by real scalar coefficients. Lengths 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 16, 32, and 64 and four signal families yield 524 coefficients per precision. The families are impulses, deterministic signed values, a constant offset, and alternating signs. A final uint32 count of 12 precedes f32 angle/sine/cosine triples, including positive/negative zero and arguments up to magnitude 1000.

The upstream DCT uses fastapprox's f32 fastcosfull even with FP_TYPE=double. Replacing it with a standard-library cosine would change the transform. The Rust implementation retains these coefficients, sign-bit handling, range reduction, multiplication/addition order, and double-precision square-root normalization. The approximation gives cos(0) about 0.9999864; the constant-signal DC coefficient retains that deviation from an ideal orthonormal DCT. Small-angle sine/cosine comparisons against standard trigonometry have a measured maximum absolute error of about 3.96e-5 across 2,001 angles between -4*pi and 4*pi. The accuracy test bound is 1e-4 and does not claim accurate large-angle range reduction. Empty DCT inputs and nonfinite/out-of-range approximate-trigonometry arguments return errors instead of the C implementation's invalid indexing or float-to-int conversion.

Across Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686, every tested DCT coefficient and approximation bit pattern matches C exactly. All fifteen integration tests pass on each target. The kernel comparison thresholds are 2e-7 for f32 and 1e-15 for f64 after normalizing by max(1, maximum input magnitude) times sqrt(length). These are scoped DCT thresholds, not complete feature-extraction tolerances.

The CZT fixtures c-czt-f32.bin and c-czt-f64.bin use tests/reference/czt_oracle.c against the pinned unmodified ciglet.c and Ooura FFT source, with the same -O2 section-removal flags as the preceding drivers. Substitute the driver and output filenames in the inverse DFT command above. CZT1 begins with little-endian uint32 scalar byte width and record count. Each of 1,200 records contains uint32 length/scenario/component-mask/inverse fields, the angular step in the selected precision, and interleaved output real/imaginary scalars. The reference contains 64,320 scalar outputs per precision. Lengths 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 11, 16, 31, 64, and 127 include prime and non-power-of-two cases. Three input families and all four component-presence combinations are tested with both directions and five grids: 2*pi/n, zero, 0.125, -0.25, and 2*pi/(1.5*n).

The Rust plan caches the FFT of the symmetric chirp kernel and reuses its work and scratch storage. The transform_into operation allocates no buffers. Chirp phases retain C's double expression followed by FP_TYPE storage; convolution uses the original twice-next-power-of-two padding. An unnormalized inverse FFT permits post-chirp multiplication before division by padded length, preserving the original normalization order. Inverse CZT negates the step and additionally divides by the signal length, as in the upstream wrapper; this is a true inverse on orthogonal DFT grids, not on arbitrary grids. Independent tests compare ordinary DFT grids to FFT results and round trips, and arbitrary grids to direct complex sums. Plan reuse, absent inputs, shape errors leaving output unchanged, overflow, and invalid phase domains are covered.

Across the five required native targets, all nineteen integration tests pass. Maximum absolute differences are of 1.7385095357894897e-2 for f32 and 7.275957614183426e-11 for f64. Maximum normalized errors are 1.7879210911753935e-7 and 3.5518465287690634e-16. Normalization uses max(1, maximum input component magnitude) times signal length for forward transforms, or the same input magnitude for inverse transforms. Measured kernel thresholds are 5e-7 for f32 and 2e-15 for f64. Complete speech-feature and inference tolerances remain to be validated.

The synthesis fixtures c-synthesis-f32.bin and c-synthesis-f64.bin use tests/reference/synthesis_oracle.c against the pinned unmodified header and source, with the same -O2 section-removal flags as preceding drivers. Substitute the driver and executable/fixture filenames in the inverse DFT command above. SYN1 begins with little-endian uint32 scalar byte width and record count. Each of 48 records contains uint32 single/length/sample-rate/tone-count fields, frequency/amplitude/center-phase scalar triples for each tone, and the output samples. Lengths 2, 3, 5, 16, 31, 128, 512, and 1001 and six scenarios yield 10,188 samples per precision. Sample rates alternate between 16000 and 44100. Cases cover unit-amplitude original single-tone generation, negative frequency and amplitude, three ordered tones, DC/Nyquist components, and empty tone lists.

The scalar recurrence retains C's double step expression, FP_TYPE step/phase storage, double cosine and initial amplitude multiplication, and FP_TYPE recurrence and summation order. Only two previous samples per tone are stored; the original length-sized temporary waveform is unnecessary. Phase refers to sample floor(length/2), including odd lengths. Single-tone generation intentionally corrects the original ignored amplitude. Original single-tone C fixtures use only unit amplitude; independent centered cosine checks validate the correction for zero, fractional, negative, and greater-than-one amplitudes. Zero/one sample handling and invalid parameter/rate/dimension checks have independent regressions.

Across all five required native targets, all twenty-three integration tests pass. All tested f32 synthesis samples match C exactly; maximum f64 normalized error is 3.1086244689504383e-15. Normalization uses max(1, sum of absolute tone amplitudes). Scoped acceptance thresholds are 2e-7 for f32 and 2e-14 for f64. The recurrence's original long-signal rounding behavior remains, so these thresholds do not assert equivalence to direct trigonometric evaluation for all lengths.

The WAVE fixtures c-wave-f32.bin and c-wave-f64.bin use tests/reference/wave_oracle.c, the pinned unmodified external/wavfile.c, and gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float/double -I<upstream> driver.c <upstream>/external/wavfile.c -lm. Invoke the executable with the fixture destination path. The original source emits unchecked-fread warnings; no warning-free C build is claimed. Each WAV1 fixture begins with uint32 scalar byte width and record count, then 36 records of uint32 WAVE byte length, raw WAVE bytes, and seven C-decoded scalar samples. All integers are little-endian; reference generation runs on Ubuntu x86_64.

Cases cover PCM 8/16/24/32 and IEEE float 32/64, mono/stereo, and fmt lengths 16/18/40. Extensible cases use standard PCM/float GUIDs. Right-channel samples differ from left to verify the original left-channel selection. Every Rust sample is independently checked against integer normalization or encoded float values. The f32 reference has 140 unchanged and 112 correction-designated samples; the f64 reference has 168 unchanged and 84 correction-designated samples. Correction groups include PCM8 bias, extensible PCM, and f32 PCM32 signed cancellation; some individual values in those groups already agree. These groups are not represented as unchanged-C matches.

Independent tests cover unknown odd chunks containing fake data magic, all truncation positions of a small WAVE, frame budgets, odd final legacy data without padding, empty input, a 128-bit PCM minimum, partial frames, nonzero stream offsets, invalid metadata, duplicate format chunks, path-based reading, injected I/O errors, and borrowed stream survival. The reader supports byte-aligned PCM containers up to 128 bits without fixed-buffer overflow; these additional widths are independently tested at the 128-bit minimum rather than claimed as exhaustive unchanged-C parity. Mono PCM WAVE writing is now covered by the additional fixtures below.

All twenty-eight integration tests passed on Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686. After the final checked-padding-offset change, the five WAVE tests were rerun and passed on all five targets. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied passed.

The PCM writer fixtures c-wave-write-f32.bin and c-wave-write-f64.bin use tests/reference/wave_write_oracle.c and the pinned unmodified external/wavfile.c with gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float/double -I<upstream> driver.c <upstream>/external/wavfile.c -lm. Each WVW1 fixture contains scalar byte width and a count of twelve records. Records contain uint32 bit depth/sample rate/sample count, the input scalars, uint32 WAVE byte count, and the complete C-written WAVE. Cases cover PCM8/16/24/32 at 22050 Hz with zero, eight, and nine samples. Signed fractional samples, including a small negative value, stay within the C implementation's defined float-to-int conversion range. All integer fields and reference floating-point values are little-endian.

WriteOptions::legacy reproduces these complete files byte for byte for f32 and f64, including original PCM8 quantization and omitted odd-data padding. Signed PCM16/24/32 quantization preserves multiplication in FP_TYPE before truncation. The standard default corrects PCM8 silence to 128, clips extrema before converting to an integer, and pads odd data while retaining the valid-data byte count. It never evaluates C's undefined out-of-range integer casts; undefined C outputs are not used as normative fixtures. In particular, f32 conversion of the PCM32 maximum scale rounds to 2^31, so positive unit samples must be clipped to INT32_MAX before conversion.

Independent regressions verify centered PCM8 bytes, correct RIFF/data lengths and padding, safe extrema in each signed depth, error propagation after partial writes, finite sample and parameter validation before output, preservation of existing file contents on validation failure, file write/read operation, and explicit legacy options. Path writers use BufWriter and explicitly flush; borrowed writers remain owned and flushed by their callers. Oversized RIFF/byte-rate arithmetic is checked. This implements the original mono PCM writer; floating-point WAVE output was not provided by the original writer.

All thirty-three integration tests pass on Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686 after adding PCM writing. Legacy writer fixtures match C byte for byte on every target. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass.

The full window fixtures c-window-f32.bin and c-window-f64.bin use tests/reference/window_oracle.c against the unmodified pinned ciglet.h. Compile with gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float/double -I<upstream> driver.c -lm and invoke with the destination binary path. WIN1 contains uint32 scalar byte width and record count, followed by uint32 window/approximate/length fields and scalar weights. Seven window families, two modes, and lengths 2, 3, 5, 8, 16, 31, 128, and 1024 yield 112 records and 17,038 weights per precision. The Boxcar family has the same implementation in both modes. Integers are explicitly little-endian in Rust; fixtures are generated on little-endian Ubuntu x86_64.

Window::generate_with adds fallible f32/f64 and level-two generation while retaining the precise f32 convenience API. Hann/Hamming retain symmetric divisors; Blackman/Harris/Nuttall retain periodic divisors. Accurate cosine sums round stored coefficients to FP_TYPE before their double arithmetic. Approximate Harris/Nuttall sums retain FP_TYPE products and additions. Approximate Hann retains C's f32 integer-one subtraction before double multiplication by 0.5, even for f64 output. MLT sine level two preserves its f32 approximation. Blackman level two remains identical to accurate Blackman because the original macro hardcodes cos_3. Empty/singleton unity corrections remain documented; oversized lengths and allocation failures return errors in the fallible API.

The expanded MLT-sine corpus exposed a one-ULP error in this port's shortened quintic coefficient literal. It is corrected to the same binary32 value as the source constant; the earlier sparse approximation and DCT cases had not exposed it. Approximate f64 window comparisons detect any binary32 drift without hiding it behind a single-precision tolerance. Across Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686, all f32 weights match exactly. Maximum f64 absolute error is 2.220446049250313e-16. Scoped bounds are 1e-7 for f32 and 1e-15 for f64. Symmetry, approximation differences, exact Blackman alias behavior, legacy convenience API agreement, and empty/singleton/range behavior have independent regressions.

All thirty-six integration tests pass on these five native targets after the window expansion and coefficient correction. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass.

The forward-STFT reference fixtures c-stft-f32.bin and c-stft-f64.bin are generated by tests/reference/stft_oracle.c against the pinned unmodified ciglet.c and external/fftsg_h.c. Build with gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float/double -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -I<upstream> driver.c <upstream>/ciglet.c <upstream>/external/fftsg_h.c -Wl,--gc-sections -lm. OpenMP and fast-math are disabled. The forward Rust implementation and measured comparisons are described below. These fixtures do not cover inverse STFT.

STF1 contains uint32 scalar byte width and record count. Each of 480 records has six uint32 fields: window, approximate, subtract-mean, variable-length, signal scenario, and output mask. Two FP_TYPE scalars follow: normalization and total window weight. Frame-major/bin-major scalars follow for four frames and seventeen bins, with magnitude when mask bit zero is set and phase when bit one is set. The five windows are boxcar, hanning, hamming, blackman, and blackman_harris. Both optimization modes, mean subtraction choices, fixed/variable windows, three signal families, and four optional-output masks are covered. Centers are -3, 5, 13, 21; fixed windows have length sixteen, variable windows have lengths eight, twelve, sixteen, twenty; FFT length is thirty-two. The input has twenty-seven samples: an impulse of 0.75 at index eleven, a nine-sample repeating signed ramp with step 0.125, or constant 2.0. Fixed-window cases request both factors; variable-window cases omit them to avoid upstream first-window reuse. The fixture contains 32,640 spectral scalars plus 960 factor scalars per precision. Phase at zero or near-zero magnitudes needs separate assessment rather than an unconditional absolute-phase tolerance.

Source inspection identifies separate corrections requiring independent regressions: odd analysis windows discard their final sample; factor requests reuse the first window for variable lengths; normalization reads center[1] without validating frame count or positive hop; and inverse fade lengths can exceed the transform buffer. The inverse also overwrites the Nyquist bin with the preceding bin through complete_symm/complete_asymm. This last behavior needs explicit compatibility and correctness analysis before choosing an inverse default. Forward-STFT fixtures do not establish inverse behavior or end-to-end reconstruction.

StftPlan::analyze now implements forward analysis for f32/f64 with a reusable FFT plan, frame/spectrum buffers, and cached most-recent window. AnalysisOptions preserves optional magnitude and phase outputs and mean subtraction. Flattened output is frame-major; positive explicit normalization spacing replaces the unsafe implicit center[1] access. The first window's total weight and overlap sum are retained independently of later variable windows. All input shapes and nonfinite samples are validated; empty analysis has no factors. The corrected odd-window arrangement retains every sample; variable windows generate their own weights even when factors are requested. These corrections have independent tests alongside centered edge padding.

Windows MSVC x86_64 reference comparison measures maximum normalized magnitude errors of 7.078051567077637e-7 for f32 and 1.7763568394002505e-15 for f64. Magnitude bounds are 2e-6 and 2e-14. Circular phase error is assessed as 2*abs(sin((actual-reference)/2))*magnitude, normalized by max(1, maximum magnitude in that frame). This measures the displacement of the polar spectrum and avoids treating unstable phase in small sidelobes as equal to strong components. Maximum weighted errors are 2.3841857910156194e-7 and 4.440892098500626e-16, within the same scoped bounds. For diagnostics, unweighted circular maxima above magnitude 1e-6 are 9.789466857910154e-4 and 4.787725771393525e-12 radians. The 3,904 phase values below magnitude 1e-6 are excluded from angular comparisons; all requested magnitude values are still compared. Optional output arrays match a repeated full-output analysis exactly. All thirty-nine integration tests passed on Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686. The five-target worst-case weighted phase errors are 2.3841857910156197e-7 and 4.440892098500626e-16. The 32-bit targets have larger unweighted sidelobe phase maxima, 6.53044879436493e-3 and 7.30304705598428e-12 radians, while meeting the weighted bounds. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass. Inverse STFT and convenience wrapper coverage remain pending.

Primary implementation references: https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.try_reserve_exact and https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/primitive.slice.html#method.fill. Storage is fallibly reserved before initialization and existing spectral buffers are cleared in place.

The inverse-STFT fixtures c-istft-f32.bin and c-istft-f64.bin use tests/reference/istft_oracle.c with the same pinned unmodified ciglet.c/external/fftsg_h.c and compilation flags as forward STFT. IST1 contains uint32 scalar width and 288-record count. Each record has uint32 FFT length, frame count, fade length, signed-offset bits, and scenario, then FP_TYPE normalization. Frame-major/bin-major input magnitude and phase pairs follow, then uint32 output count and output samples. FFT lengths 32/64, frame counts 2/5, fades 0/1/8/32, offsets -3/0/5, three spectral scenarios, and normalizations 0.75/2 are covered. Hop is four; window factor is eight and zero-padding factor is one/two. Inputs include isolated Nyquist energy, a varying magnitude/phase spectrum, and one nonzero interior bin. There are 4,224 output samples per precision. Multi-byte data are little-endian; offsets are read as signed i32.

StftPlan::synthesize reuses FFT, spectrum, and frame storage. It retains FP_TYPE products with f32 level-two sine/cosine, inverse normalization, centered shifting, accurate Hann endpoint fading, serial frame-order overlap-add, and hop*frames+offset output length. NyquistPolicy::Legacy reproduces the original complete_symm/complete_asymm preceding-bin substitution, including its imaginary component. NyquistPolicy::Preserve is the default correction: Nyquist real energy is retained, and DC/Nyquist imaginary components are zeroed for real reconstruction. No change to the original global symmetry helpers is claimed; their separate public coverage remains pending. Invalid spectral shapes, nonfinite values, zero spacing/normalization, out-of-range lengths, and overlong fades return errors. Overlapping valid endpoint fades retain the original sequential double multiplication. Empty frame sets are safe.

Initial Windows MSVC x86_64 unchanged-C comparisons in Legacy mode measure maximum normalized error 5.960464477539063e-8 for f32 and 2.7755575615628914e-16 for f64; scoped bounds are 2e-7 and 2e-15. Repeated synthesis with a reused plan is exactly equal. An independent isolated-Nyquist test verifies the alternating waveform in corrected mode and complete loss of that waveform in Legacy mode. The expected amplitude includes upstream approximate cos(0), rather than assuming exact unity. Invalid inputs, empty output, and zero-padded tails are independently tested.

FrameGrid/analyze_regular/synthesize_regular implement stft, stft_2 and istft workflows. Blackman optimization modes match exactly as in C; explicit regular centers/windows produce identical analysis. A sine signal passes through analysis and corrected synthesis with interior maximum error 1.3566459428071553e-5 on initial Windows x86_64 testing, below 1e-4. This scoped reconstruction uses the retained upstream polar approximation and excludes boundary truncation; it is not full real-audio SHIRO acceptance. Single-frame normalization is supported safely. All forty-three integration tests passed on Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686. Five-target maximum inverse normalized errors are 1.1920928955078125e-7 for f32 and 3.3306690738754696e-16 for f64; worst interior reconstruction error is 1.3566486903870967e-5. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass.

The frequency fixtures c-frequency-f32.bin and c-frequency-f64.bin use tests/reference/frequency_oracle.c and the pinned unmodified ciglet.h/fastapprox-all.h. Build with gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float/double -I<upstream> driver.c -lm. FRQ1 has uint32 scalar width and twelve-record count, followed by six FP_TYPE fields per record: input Hz, mel, mel-to-Hz round trip, Bark, Bark-to-Hz round trip, and equal-loudness weight. Frequencies range from zero to 96,000 Hz. A uint32 spacing count of five follows; each spacing has uint32 interval count and intervals+1 FP_TYPE points for bounds 50/8000 Hz and interval counts 1/2/5/20/40. The final sections contain uint32 counts of twelve each, with f32 triples for input/log2/log and f32 quadruples for input/exp2/exp/pow(10,input/40), independent of FP_TYPE. All values are little-endian.

The frequency module retains approximate log/exp for mel conversion, double asinh/sinh for Bark, FP_TYPE squaring for equal-loudness weighting, and FP_TYPE interpolation for mel-space points. These are prerequisites for filterbank construction; filterbank construction and application remain pending. Each fixture verifies 133 conversion/spacing outputs plus sixty approximation outputs. Initial Windows MSVC x86_64 results match all f32 conversion/spacing outputs exactly. f64 maximum normalized error is 1.5158245029548806e-16; all mel-space points match exactly for both precisions. All sixty approximation outputs match C bit patterns exactly. Scoped conversion bounds are 1e-7 for f32 and 1e-15 for f64.

The level-two approximation retains the original -126 base-two exponent clamp. Invalid log domains, nonfinite exponents, exponent overflow and invalid integer-bit conversion domains return errors. Frequency outputs are checked for finiteness; zero intervals and reversed mel-space bounds are rejected. Signed Bark coordinates still round-trip. Independent tests check zero equal-loudness weight, monotonic spacing, signed Bark round trips, invalid domains, and the underflow clamp. Across 1,001 sampled points, maximum absolute natural-log error is 1.0371208e-4 and maximum relative natural-exponential error is 6.494367e-5; both are below 2e-4. These accuracy checks do not replace unchanged-C bit comparisons. All forty-seven integration tests passed on Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686. f32 conversion/spacing outputs and all sixty approximation outputs are exact on each target; the worst f64 normalized conversion error is 3.789561257387201e-16. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass.

The new bit approximations are adapted from the same Paul Mineiro fastapprox source with the existing retained BSD notice. Safe conversion follows the Rust primary reference https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.f32.html#method.to_bits and https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.f32.html#method.from_bits. LN_2 and LOG2_E use standard f32 constants with the same bit patterns as the original decimal constants, verified by the C corpus.

The filterbank fixtures c-filterbank-f32.bin and c-filterbank-f64.bin use tests/reference/filterbank_oracle.c with unmodified pinned ciglet.c. Build with gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float/double -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -I<upstream> driver.c <upstream>/ciglet.c -Wl,--gc-sections -lm. FBK1 contains uint32 scalar width and record count of 72. Each record starts with uint32 bank kind/bin count/channel count and FP_TYPE Nyquist Hz. Channel records have uint32 lower/upper support and bin-count FP_TYPE response values. For each compression mode, three single-spectrum outputs and three-frame spectrogram outputs follow, each frame having channel-count FP_TYPE values. Cases cover empty, warped mel, default mel and PLP banks; 257/513/1025 bins; 4/20/32 channels; Nyquist 8000/11025 Hz. Mel bounds are 50..Nyquist; custom mel scale is 0.85 with width 120 Hz, while the convenience mel bank uses scale 1 and width 400 Hz. Spectrum inputs are zero, a positive seventeen-bin repeating ramp with step 0.125, and amplitude two at bin-count/3. Compression order is logarithmic followed by PLP power 0.33. Integers and scalars are little-endian. There are 804,160 response coefficients and 16,128 compressed outputs per precision.

FilterBank retains source scalar frequency coordinates, integer floor/ceil/round supports, triangular coefficients, Bark mask and equal-loudness arithmetic, and FP_TYPE accumulation order. Its compression retains f32 fastlog(sum+1e-15) or double pow(sum,0.33), including in the double build. The original unused FFT/sample-rate application parameters are replaced by the bank's checked shape. Owned storage, read-only response/support access and validated set_channel replace unvalidated pointer ownership and manual destruction. Custom signed responses remain supported; invalid compression domains return errors. Spectrogram processing has one output allocation and shares the spectrum accumulation helper.

Initial Windows MSVC x86_64 response and output comparisons match every f32 value exactly. Maximum normalized f64 response/output errors are 1.1102230246251565e-16 and 2.1915715056264076e-16. Scoped response bounds are 2e-7/2e-14; output bounds are 2e-6/2e-13. Every channel support matches C exactly. Independent tests cover safe corrected small grids, extreme positive warp factors, unit response at a zero-centered first band, response bounds, custom support exclusion, replacement validation before mutation, finite/shape validation, empty frames and zero channels. Single-spectrum output matches flattened spectrogram output exactly. All fifty integration tests passed on Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686. f32 response and output values match exactly across all targets. Worst normalized f64 response/output errors are 1.1102230246251565e-16 and 2.206700641277429e-16. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass.

The cepstral fixtures c-cepstrum-f32.bin and c-cepstrum-f64.bin use tests/reference/cepstrum_oracle.c with pinned unmodified ciglet.c/ciglet.h. Build with gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float/double -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -I<upstream> driver.c <upstream>/ciglet.c -Wl,--gc-sections -lm. CEP1 contains uint32 scalar width and 48-record count. Each record has uint32 band count/order/include-DC fields, three frame-major input rows of band-count FP_TYPE values, three complete single-frame be2cc output rows, then three complete be2ccgm output rows. Band counts are 1/2/5/12/20/40; orders are zero, one, band-count minus one, and band-count plus five. Both DC choices are covered. Frames contain zeros, constant -15 and a signed repeating ramp with step 0.25. All multibyte data are little-endian. There are 3,840 reference output coefficients per precision.

The cepstrum module retains the original approximate DCT, clamp to band-count minus one, relocation of non-DC coefficients to the beginning, and optional DC placement after the requested coefficients. band_to_cepstrum returns this requested prefix. band_to_cepstrum_legacy additionally retains the complete original band-count-sized buffer, including its unchanged DCT suffix. Flattened frame-major conversion supports multiple frames. Neither API applies an additional log to signed band features. Empty band counts, invalid matrix shapes and nonfinite features return errors; empty frame matrices with positive band count are valid.

Initial Windows MSVC x86_64 comparisons match every f32/f64 reference coefficient exactly. Single-frame results, requested prefixes and flattened rows agree; both complete C single-frame and matrix buffers are independently consumed from the fixture. Independent checks cover singleton and zero-order behavior, large requested order clamping, DC normalization, empty/invalid shapes and a silence pipeline through mel filterbank, the SHIRO -15 feature floor and 13-coefficient conversion. The pipeline checks the approximate-cosine DC value without claiming complete SHIRO tool or real-audio acceptance. All fifty-three integration tests passed on Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64 and Linux GNU x86_64/i686. All tested f32/f64 legacy cepstral coefficients match C exactly on every target. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass.

Safe overlapping coefficient relocation uses slice::copy_within, matching the primary Rust documentation at https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.slice.html#method.copy_within. Prefix shortening uses Vec::truncate and does not change retained coefficient values.


The c-filter-resample-f32.bin and c-filter-resample-f64.bin fixtures contain 300 FIR, 60 convolution and 105 resampling cases per precision from pinned unmodified C. The FRS1 layout, build command, numerical bounds and corrected boundary policy are documented in docs/filter-resample-compatibility.md. tests/reference/filter_resample_oracle.c is the reproducible driver. No C code is linked into the Rust library.

The spectral-peak-float.bin and spectral-peak-double.bin fixtures use the unchanged pinned cig_qifft body. QIF1 stores magic, uint32 scalar width and case count, then 64 records of three input scalars, fractional bin position and interpolated magnitude. All fields are little-endian. See docs/spectral-peak-compatibility.md and tests/generate_spectral_peak_reference.py for reproduction and verification.

The real-cepstrum-float.bin and real-cepstrum-double.bin fixtures use the unchanged pinned C library and header. RCP1 stores magic, uint32 scalar width and 72-case count. Each record contains uint32 FFT length and coefficient count, one-sided log spectrum, full real cepstrum, full inverse spectrum, full Legacy phase, three-frame one-sided magnitude inputs, three-frame coefficient prefixes and reconstructed one-sided magnitudes. All fields are little-endian. The corpus stores 9,432 C output scalars per precision. See docs/real-cepstrum-compatibility.md for measured bounds and tests/generate_real_cepstrum_reference.py for regeneration.

The array.bin fixture uses the unchanged pinned C row-pointer helpers and transpose dispatch. ARR1 stores magic and uint32 240-case count, followed by records of uint32 rows/columns/element-width and five row-major raw byte buffers: input, zero allocation, copied/flattened values, reshaped/flattened values and transposed/flattened values. The output shape for transpose swaps rows and columns. Element widths are 1/2/4/8 bytes; all integer fields and typed payloads are little-endian. The corpus stores 59,280 output bytes. See docs/array-compatibility.md and tests/generate_array_reference.py for exact comparisons and regeneration.

The scalar-math-float.bin and scalar-math-double.bin fixtures compile only the unchanged pinned header and fastapprox definitions. SCM1 stores magic, uint32 scalar width and 64-case count; each case contains angle/y/x, sine/cosine outputs at levels one/two/three and atan2 outputs at levels one/two/three. A uint32 16-pair count follows, with four scalars per comparison record: first/second operands and source min/max outputs. All fields are little-endian. The corpus contains 608 reference outputs per precision. Comparison and approximation bytes are exact; only specified double libm fields permit a measured one-ULP regeneration difference. See docs/scalar-math-compatibility.md and tests/generate_scalar_math_reference.py.

The sinc-float.bin and sinc-double.bin fixtures compile the unchanged pinned header. SNC1 stores magic, uint32 scalar width and 192-case count, followed by four scalars per record: length, angular frequency, source safe_aliased_sinc output and source safe_aliased_dsinc output. All fields are little-endian; there are 384 reference outputs per precision. Windows Zig and Linux GCC regenerate identical bytes. See docs/sinc-compatibility.md and tests/generate_sinc_reference.py for measured Legacy bounds and analytic default tests.

The distance-float.bin and distance-double.bin fixtures compile the unchanged pinned header and fastapprox definitions. ISD1 stores magic, uint32 scalar width and 53-case count, followed by records containing uint32 bin count, source scalars, reference scalars and the source approximate log-mean Itakura-Saito result. All fields are little-endian. Edge records deliberately retain C artifacts from zero, subnormal, infinity and NaN intermediate values; external input arrays remain finite and nonnegative. See docs/distance-compatibility.md and tests/generate_distance_reference.py for regeneration and corrected analytic tests.
